# Quality Checks

> A nine-phase final-line-of-defense pipeline for code that ships. Composes security analysis (claude-code-security-review), design rigour (impeccable), and industry UI intelligence (ui-ux-pro-max-skill). The deterministic gate runs 11 regex-detectable rules in CI; the slash command runs LLM judgment on the rest. MIT licensed, free.

## What it does

Quality Checks reads a branch diff and emits one markdown verdict per the rubric. Five scoring dimensions (Anti-Pattern, Design System, Accessibility, Performance, Resilience), total out of 20. Five bands (Excellent, Good, Acceptable, Poor, Critical). Security verdict and deterministic-gate verdict override the band.

The deterministic gate is a 250-line bash script (quality-checks/scripts/check.sh) that catches eleven regex-detectable patterns: side-stripe borders, gradient text, pure black or pure white, layout-property animation, outline: none, div onClick, em dashes, banned diction, throat-clearing openers, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html and Svelte @html. Self-tested against 13 fixtures.

The LLM judgment phases run through the Claude Code slash command /quality-checks. They cover security review (Phase 1), anti-pattern audit (Phase 2 subjective subset), design-system drift (Phase 3), accessibility heuristics (Phase 4), performance audit (Phase 5), resilience review (Phase 6), structural editorial review (Phase 7), and stack-specific idioms (Phase 8).

## Use this when

You want to evaluate whether a frontend branch is ready to merge against five dimensions: AI-pattern density, design-system conformance, accessibility, performance, resilience. You want a deterministic gate that runs in CI in under a second. You want a composable system that does not replace your existing security review or design system.

## Do not use this for

Running tests against a deployed application. Penetration testing. Auto-merging or auto-fixing code. Replacing human code review on architectural decisions.
